items.value: Only two of the four — Hedge Funds and Venture Capital — are Alternative Investment Funds
items.reasoning: Under the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012, an AIF is a privately pooled investment vehicle that is not covered by the Mutual Fund or Collective Investment Scheme regulations. Venture Capital Funds fall in Category I and Hedge Funds in Category III. Bonds and Stocks are ordinary securities — the traditional asset classes against which 'alternative' is defined — and are not AIFs, so exactly two of the four qualify.

items.value: Only I and II — buying/selling Government bonds and buying/selling foreign currency — are RBI income sources
items.reasoning: The RBI earns interest and trading gains on its rupee securities portfolio (open market operations) and interest plus realised gains on its foreign currency assets, so I and II are genuine income heads. Pension fund management belongs to the PFRDA, not the RBI, and the RBI does not lend to private companies — its lending is to banks and to governments. Printing and distributing currency is a large item of RBI *expenditure*, not income, which is the trap in statement V.

items.value: Only two rows are correctly matched — the Directorate of Enforcement row is wrong because the ED works under the Department of Revenue, not the Ministry of Home Affairs
items.reasoning: The Directorate of Enforcement does enforce the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 (along with PMLA and FEMA), but it is a specialised financial investigation agency under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance — not under any Internal Security Division of the MHA — so row I is mismatched. The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence enforces the Customs Act, 1962 under the Department of Revenue, and the Directorate General of Systems and Data Management performs data analytics for tax administration under the same Department, so rows II and III are correct.

items.value: Only statement II is correct — BRSR disclosures are largely non-financial
items.reasoning: The Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report is mandated by SEBI, not the Reserve Bank of India, and it applies to the top listed companies by market capitalisation rather than to all listed companies — statement I is wrong on both counts. Statement II is correct: the BRSR captures environmental, social and governance parameters such as emissions, energy and water use, employee welfare and board oversight, which are non-financial disclosures.

items.value: Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct — allied activities are taxable, while rural agricultural land is not a capital asset
items.reasoning: Section 2(1A) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 defines agricultural income narrowly around operations on land, and settled practice excludes poultry farming, dairying, fishing and wool/sheep rearing — such income is taxable as business income, so Statement I is wrong. Statement II is correct: Section 2(14) expressly excludes from 'capital asset' agricultural land in India that lies outside the specified municipal limits and distances, so transfer of rural agricultural land attracts no capital gains tax.

items.value: Statements I and III are correct; India is not resource-rich in all 30 identified critical minerals
items.reasoning: India joined the US-led Minerals Security Partnership in 2023, so I is correct, and the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2023 inserted the critical and strategic minerals list and empowered the Central Government to exclusively auction mining leases and composite licences for them, so III is correct. Statement II is false and is in fact the reason the exercise was undertaken — India identified 30 critical minerals precisely because it is heavily import-dependent for lithium, cobalt, nickel and rare earths.

items.value: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both explain Statement I
items.reasoning: Statement I is correct — bondholders bear less risk than stockholders. Statement II is correct and explanatory: a bondholder is a creditor with a contractual claim to fixed interest and principal, while a stockholder is a residual owner whose return depends on profits. Statement III is also correct and explanatory: in liquidation, debt claims rank ahead of equity, so bondholders are repaid first. Since both II and III are true and each independently accounts for the lower risk in I, option A holds; C fails because it requires only one of them to be correct.

items.value: Statements I and II are correct; statement III is false because SEBI does regulate and warn on options trading
items.reasoning: India has accounted for the overwhelming majority of global equity option contracts traded by volume in recent years, so I is correct, and India's market capitalisation overtook Hong Kong's to become the world's fourth largest in early 2024, so II is correct. Statement III is plainly wrong: SEBI has published studies on losses in the futures and options segment, issued investor cautions and taken action against unregistered investment advisers and 'finfluencers'.

items.value: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both explain Statement I
items.reasoning: A circular economy reduces greenhouse gas emissions (Statement I). Statement II is correct and explanatory — reusing, recycling and remanufacturing cuts demand for virgin raw materials, and extraction plus primary processing of ores and fossil feedstock is among the most emission-intensive stages of any supply chain. Statement III is likewise correct and explanatory — less scrap and rejects per unit of output means less material and energy consumed for the same product, and less waste sent to landfill where it would decompose to methane. Both causal links are genuine, so A rather than B or C; the judgement call is whether the examiner regards both as explanatory, which is why this is not marked HIGH.

items.value: Statements I and II are correct; interest received on loans is a revenue receipt and creates no liability
items.reasoning: Statement I states the standard definition — a capital receipt either creates a liability for the Government or reduces its assets. Statement II follows from it: borrowings create a liability and disinvestment reduces the Government's asset holdings, so both are capital receipts. Statement III is wrong: interest received on loans advanced by the Government neither creates a liability nor reduces an asset, and is therefore classified as a revenue receipt.

items.value: Both statements about Raja Ram Mohan Roy are correct
items.reasoning: Roy had deep regard for Eastern philosophical traditions — he studied Sanskrit, Persian and Arabic, translated the Vedas and several Upanishads into Bengali and English, and grounded his religious reform in the Vedanta, so statement I is correct. Statement II is equally correct: he championed rational and scientific enquiry over blind custom, campaigned against sati and for widow remarriage and women's property rights, and argued for the dignity and social equality of men and women alike.

items.value: Three of the four were part of the Non-Cooperation Programme; the retention of titles was not — the programme demanded their surrender
items.reasoning: Boycott of law courts by lawyers and litigants and boycott of foreign cloth were core planks of the programme, so I qualifies; Gandhi made observance of strict non-violence a binding condition, which is why he withdrew the movement after Chauri Chaura, so II qualifies; and the constructive side of the programme expressly provided for panchayats to arbitrate disputes as a substitute for the boycotted courts, so IV qualifies. Statement III inverts the programme — participants were called upon to surrender titles and honorary offices, not to retain them unused — leaving three correct.

items.value: Araghatta was a large wheel with earthen pots tied to the outer ends of its spokes
items.reasoning: The word itself carries the description: 'ara' means spoke and 'ghatta' means pot, so the araghatta is the pot-garland wheel — the noria or Persian wheel — in which pots fixed to the rim or spoke-ends fill at the bottom of the rotation and empty into a channel at the top. Option A describes the mot or charas leather-bag lift, and options C and D describe simpler bucket lifts, none of which involve a spoked wheel carrying pots.

items.value: Mahendravarman I of the Pallava dynasty
items.reasoning: Mahendravarman I (c. 600–630 CE) wrote the satirical Sanskrit farce Mattavilasa Prahasana, from which the title 'Mattavilasa' derives, and his inscriptions — notably at the Mandagapattu and Trichy rock-cut cave temples — record the birudas 'Vichitrachitta' (of curious mind) and 'Gunabhara'. Simhavishnu was his grandfather, Narasimhavarman I his son who bore 'Mamalla' and 'Vatapikonda', and Simhavarman an earlier Pallava.

items.value: Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya)
items.reasoning: Fa-hien travelled in India roughly between 399 and 414 CE, which falls squarely in the reign of Chandragupta II, and his account 'Fo-kuo-ki' describes a peaceful and prosperous Madhyadesha of that period. Samudragupta preceded him, while Kumaragupta I and Skandagupta ruled later — Hiuen Tsang, the other famous Chinese pilgrim, came much later still, in Harshavardhana's reign.

items.value: Rajendra I of the Chola dynasty
items.reasoning: Rajendra I launched the celebrated naval expedition across the Bay of Bengal against the Sailendra kingdom of Srivijaya around 1025 CE, sacking Kadaram and other ports across the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra — the only major overseas military campaign mounted by an Indian power in this period. Amoghavarsha, Prataparudra and Vishnuvardhana were all inland rulers with no naval reach into South-East Asia.

items.value: Only two pairs are correct — Asmaka–Godavari and Kosala–Sarayu
items.reasoning: Asmaka (Assaka) lay on the Godavari with its capital at Potana, and Kosala was watered by the Sarayu, which divided it into a northern half around Shravasti and a southern half around Ayodhya — so pairs I and IV are correct. Kamboja lay in the far north-west beyond the Indus, in the Kabul–Rajapura tract, whereas the Vipas (Beas) flows through Punjab, so pair II is wrong. Avanti occupied Malwa with Ujjayini on the Shipra and Mahishmati on the Narmada, while the Mahanadi drains Chhattisgarh and Odisha, so pair III is wrong.

items.value: Lahore
items.reasoning: Vishnu Digambar Paluskar founded the first Gandharva Mahavidyalaya at Lahore on 5 May 1901, funding it by public subscription so that music teaching would move out of hereditary gharana households and into an open school. He later shifted his base to Bombay in 1908, where a second Gandharva Mahavidyalaya was established, which is the usual source of confusion with the other options.

items.value: District-level administration
items.reasoning: Ashoka's Rock Edict III directs that the Yuktas, Rajukas and Pradeshikas set out on a quinquennial tour (anusamyana) of their charges to propagate Dhamma and attend to administration, and Pillar Edict IV assigns the Rajukas authority over the people of the countryside. The Pradeshika headed a district, the Rajuka handled land survey, assessment and judicial work in rural tracts, and the Yuktas were subordinate revenue and accounts officials attached to them — the three together form the district tier, below the provincial governors (Kumaras) and above the village headman.

items.value: Both statements about the Non-Cooperation Movement are correct
items.reasoning: At the Nagpur session of December 1920 the Congress amended its creed to the attainment of Swaraj by all legitimate and peaceful means, replacing the earlier goal of self-government within the Empire, so statement I is correct. Statement II is also correct: the programme was designed in stages, with the milder forms of non-cooperation first and the militant forms — civil disobedience including refusal to pay taxes — held back for a later stage, to be resorted to only if Swaraj did not come within a year and the Government met the movement with repression.

items.value: Only four — Bulgaria, Croatia, Sweden and North Macedonia — are NATO members
items.reasoning: Bulgaria joined NATO in 2004, Croatia in 2009, North Macedonia in 2020 and Sweden in March 2024, giving four members from this list. Austria has been constitutionally neutral since 1955 and has never joined, and Serbia has declared a policy of military neutrality and participates only through Partnership for Peace, so neither is a member.

items.value: Only four — Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Venezuela — have the Andes passing through them
items.reasoning: The Andes run the length of western South America through seven countries: Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina. Of the six listed, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Venezuela are on that list, making four. Brazil lies east of the range and is drained by the Amazon and its shield uplands, and Paraguay is a landlocked lowland country of the Chaco and Parana basin with no Andean territory.

items.value: None of the three water bodies is crossed by the equator
items.reasoning: Lake Tanganyika lies entirely in the southern hemisphere, its northern tip reaching only to about 3 degrees south — it is Lake Victoria, further north-east, that the equator crosses. Tonle Sap is in Cambodia at roughly 13 degrees north, and the Patos Lagoon lies in Rio Grande do Sul in southern Brazil at about 30 to 31 degrees south. The equator therefore passes through none of them.

items.value: All three statements about turmeric are correct
items.reasoning: India is by a wide margin the world's largest producer of turmeric, accounting for the bulk of global output, and is also the largest exporter, so I is correct. More than thirty varieties of turmeric are cultivated across some twenty Indian states, so II is correct. Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu are the leading producing states, so III is correct as well. The statement carrying most of the uncertainty is II, since it turns on a specific varietal count rather than on a general fact.

items.value: All three are cited as evidence for continental drift
items.reasoning: All three are standard evidences advanced for Wegener's continental drift. The belt of ancient rocks about 2,000 million years old on the Brazilian coast matches the corresponding belt in western Africa, indicating the two coasts were once joined. The placer gold deposits of the Ghana coast have no source rock in Ghana and are traced to the Brazil plateau, which would have lain alongside. And the Gondwana sequence of sediments, capped by the Glossopteris flora, recurs in six landmasses of the southern hemisphere, pointing to a single former supercontinent.
